subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce a core action-verification, fail-closed, or recovery policy when visible final text claims completed side effects without matching tool or source-delivery evidence?
rationale: The source shows the current core only gates or warns on specific delivery-tool omissions, while preventing arbitrary false action claims requires a product boundary across privacy, delivery, tool ledgers, plugin policy, and provider/runtime behavior.

options.title: Define Core Verification Policy
options.body: Specify which side effects must be evidenced, how recovery or diagnostics work, and which privacy/source-reply invariants cannot be broken before implementing the core fix.

options.title: Limit Core To Stranded-Final Recovery
options.body: Keep #41824 open as broader design work while landing only the #85714-style missing message-tool fallback in a narrower PR.

options.title: Route Generic Claim Verification Out Of Core
options.body: Document current source-reply behavior and push arbitrary action-claim checks to a plugin, hook, or ClawHub policy while keeping core focused on delivery contracts.

recommendation.title: Define Core Verification Policy
recommendation.body: Specify which side effects must be evidenced, how recovery or diagnostics work, and which privacy/source-reply invariants cannot be broken before implementing the core fix.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent source-reply policy history and is already linked to adjacent maintainer-routing discussion for the affected behavior.
